## Findings
- claim-1: For \(a=\min(n-r-i,r-j)\), \(b=\min(i,j)\), \(J_v\subseteq H^\star(G/P_J,\mathbb Z)\cong\Lambda/I_{r,n-r}\) is generated by either Schur interval, each of cardinality \(\binom{a+b}{a}\). [source-2@L1382-L1421|claim=formal-document]
- claim-2: For a graded connected algebra \(\Lambda\) over \(R\), homogeneous generators of \(M\) are inclusion-minimal exactly when their images minimally span \(M/\Lambda_+M\); the paper specializes this with \(R=\mathbb Z\), \(\Lambda\) the symmetric functions, and \(M=J_v\). [source-2@L1520-L1540|claim=formal-document]
- claim-3: Let \((P)\) be the accepted exact integral box/Schur/Pieri presentation. Every non-source hypothesis used in the conditional \(a=1,b=2\) argument is a clause of \((P)\): integral graded Schur bases for \(A=\Lambda/I_{r,q}\) and \(J_v\), exact degreewise Schur-column lists in the \(q^r\)-box, and integral Pieri multiplication whose positive-degree product lattice is \(A_+J_v\).
- claim-4: Under \((P)\), \(a=1,b=2\) implies \[ i,j\ge2,\quad p:=q-i\ge1,\quad c:=r-j\ge1,\quad \min(i,j)=2,\quad\min(p,c)=1. \] Hence \(q,r\ge3\), and exactly the cases \(p=1,c\ge2\), \(p\ge2,c=1\), and \(p=c=1\) occur.
- claim-5: Under \((P)\), with \(d=ij\), \[ Q_d=\mathbb Z\bar x_0,\qquad Q_{d+1}=\mathbb Z\bar x_1,\qquad Q_{d+2}=\mathbb Z\bar x_2, \] where \[ x_0=s_{i^j},\quad x_1=s_{(i+1,i^{j-1})},\quad x_2=s_{((i+1)^2,i^{j-2})}, \] and \(\bar y_1=-\bar x_1,\ \bar y_2=\bar x_2\), for \[ y_1=s_{(i^j,1)},\qquad y_2=s_{(i^j,2)}. \]
- claim-6: Under \((P)\), source-backed generation by \((x_0,x_1,x_2)\) induces a graded surjection \[ \mathbb Zx_0\oplus\mathbb Zx_1\oplus\mathbb Zx_2\twoheadrightarrow Q:=J_v/A_+J_v. \] The preceding degreewise isomorphisms annihilate its homogeneous kernel, so \[ Q\cong\mathbb Z^3. \]
- claim-7: The two source-backed \(a=1,b=2\) generating families \[ F_1=(x_0,x_1,x_2),\qquad F_2=(x_0,y_1,y_2) \] map to bases of \(Q\), related by \(\operatorname{diag}(1,-1,1)\). Therefore both are inclusion-minimal.
- claim-8: **Target established internally:** the conditional qualification may be removed from the project-internal \(a=1,b=2\) conclusion, since all of its presentation hypotheses are supplied by the accepted exact integral presentation \((P)\). It cannot be removed in a standalone source-backed formulation from the supplied excerpts, which do not themselves state \((P)\).
## Strategy
Construct the required closure table as follows.

| Used step | Required hypothesis | Available grounding |
|---|---|---|
| \(F_1,F_2\) generate \(J_v\) | The two Schur-interval generation theorem; for \(a=1,b=2\), these are \((x_0,x_1,x_2)\) and \((x_0,y_1,y_2)\) | source-2@L1382-L1421 |
| \(Q=J_v/A_+J_v\) is graded and \(A/A_+\cong\mathbb Z\) | \(A\) is a connected graded integral quotient and \(A_+\) is its positive-degree ideal | Must be an explicit clause of the exact presentation |
| \(J_v\) is homogeneous and bounded below | Exact graded Schur-basis description of \(J_v\), including that no Schur class occurs below \(d=ij\) | Must be an explicit clause of the exact presentation |
| Low-degree quotient calculations | Integral Schur-column bases, integral Pieri multiplication, and equality of the displayed Pieri-row lattice with \((A_+J_v)_{d+1},(A_+J_v)_{d+2}\) | Conditional certificates: tasks 47–50 and 48 |
| Globalization from degrees \(d,d+1,d+2\) | Graded surjection \(\mathbb Zx_0\oplus\mathbb Zx_1\oplus\mathbb Zx_2\twoheadrightarrow Q\) | Source generation plus connected graded structure; conditional task 51 |
| Apply source Nakayama criterion | \(\Lambda_+J_v=A_+J_v\) | Follows if \(\pi:\Lambda\twoheadrightarrow A\) is a graded surjection with \(A_0=\mathbb Z\) |

For the last equality, under those presentation clauses,
\[
A_+=\pi(\Lambda_+).
\]
Indeed, graded surjectivity gives \(A_k=\pi(\Lambda_k)\) for every \(k>0\). Hence
\[
A_+J_v=\pi(\Lambda_+)J_v=\Lambda_+J_v,
\]
where the \(\Lambda\)-action factors through \(\pi\). Thus source-2@L1520-L1540 applies once the graded and lower-bounded hypotheses on \(J_v\) are supplied by the presentation.

\]
